title: The source reads version 1 in its metadata table and v2 in its file name
source: Recovery Workbench Notification and Correspondence Design v2.docx
description: The metadata table of the source reads 'Version | 1' and 'Date | 28 October 2026', while the file name is 'Recovery Workbench Notification and Correspondence Design v2.docx'. Two readings are possible: the metadata row was not raised when the file was reissued as version 2, or the file name is the family version and the table is the document's own issue number. The reading decides what the next version is called and which number the change log carries.
evidence: Source metadata rows 'Version | 1' and 'Date | 28 October 2026'; source file name 'Recovery Workbench Notification and Correspondence Design v2.docx'; core properties title 'Recovery Workbench Notification and Correspondence Design v2' and revision 1.
owner_role: Document owner of the notification and correspondence design
proposed: Take the file name as the family version, so this document becomes version 3, and keep the source readings in a 'Source version' row: 1, 28 October 2026. The change log carries both readings.

title: DL10 is listed open with one answer and is recorded as answered with another
source: Recovery Workbench Notification and Correspondence Design v2.docx; Recovery Workbench Decision Log v10
description: The source lists DL10 as open, reads it as 'Thai wording', and gives the fallback answer 'English drafts with Thai requested'. The Decision Log v10 records DL10 as 'Thai field names', answer A, on 5 November 2026: the business lead drafts per module one epic ahead and Legal and Compliance approve. The subject and the answer of the same decision therefore differ between the two documents.
evidence: Source section 6 row 'DL10 | Thai wording | English drafts with Thai requested'; Decision Log v10 row DL10 'Thai field names', answer A, decided 2026-11-05, document 'Error and message standard; content and label standard; functional specification per module'.
owner_role: Business lead with Legal and Compliance; document owner
proposed: Keep the source row word for word, record in section 6.1 that DL10 is answered on 5 November 2026 with answer A, and add no Thai wording in this document.

title: The Decision Log gives the letter templates to the document module, while Architecture v5 and the Ownership Map give them to rwb-comms
source: Recovery Workbench Notification and Correspondence Design v2.docx; Recovery Workbench Decision Log v10; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5; Microservice Ownership Map v1
description: The source says the Workbench holds template rows with code, version, language, product group, body and Legal approval. The Decision Log v10 records DL28 on 13 November 2026 with answer A: the document module owns the templates and the fields, and Legal approves the wording. Architecture v5 slide 41 and the Ownership Map v1 give notices, templates, merge fields and proof of delivery to P6 rwb-comms, and the P6 endpoints GET and POST /admin/templates are owned by P6. R-PREC ranks Architecture v5 above the Decision Log, so the ownership of the template and its fields is contested in the sources.
evidence: Source section 3 table; Decision Log v10 row DL28 answer A, decided 2026-11-13; Architecture v5 slide 41 ('P6 owns notices, templates, merge fields, proof of delivery') and slide 17 (P6 DB line); Ownership Map v1 sheets Tables (template, merge_field to P6) and Endpoints (admin/templates to P6).
owner_role: Product owner; service owners of P6 rwb-comms and P5 rwb-document
proposed: Follow Architecture v5 and the Ownership Map: templates and merge fields are P6 rwb_comms. Record the DL28 answer as a gap and ask the product owner to reaffirm or amend DL28 before the template story is Done.

title: The proof of delivery is named as P6 data but has no table, no DDL and no owner row
source: Recovery Workbench Notification and Correspondence Design v2.docx; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5; Microservice Ownership Map v1; Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2; Recovery Workbench Interface Specifications v4
section: 1 What is sent, 2 How a notice is produced, and 2.1
description: Architecture v5 slide 41 and slide 17 name 'proof of delivery' among the data of rwb-comms, and the source says WIN returns the barcode and then the proof of delivery in the weekly file. The Ownership Map v1 lists only notice, template and merge_field for P6; the TSD P6 object list has no proof-of-delivery table; and INT-15 carries the proof into ACE with the fields DDMMYYYY, ContractNO, Barcode, DDMMYYYY_callBack and Sent Type. No source says whether the proof is a table of its own or a set of columns on the notice.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 41 and slide 17 ('proof of delivery'); Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables (P6 rows: merge_field, notice, template); TSD P6 T3.1 (notice, template, merge_field, signature_request); Interface Specifications v4 row INT-15 payload.
owner_role: Service owner of P6 rwb-comms, with the DB story of the service
proposed: Hold the barcode, the callback date and the delivery status on the notice row, as the INT-14 and INT-15 field mapping does, and settle a separate proof table only if a DB story needs it.

title: The contact point and its consent state are a P6 feature but a P1 table, and no endpoint carries them
source: Recovery Workbench Notification and Correspondence Design v2.docx; Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3; Microservice Ownership Map v1; Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2
description: The source requires the consent of the channel to be checked before every message and says the contact rules are held as reference data. FSD P6 A2.18 makes the contact repository a P6 feature and says consent, verification and failed count are held in recovery.contact_point_ext, read from v_ace_contact. The Ownership Map v1 gives contact_point_ext to P1 rwb-source-data, and TSD P6 T5.2 says reference data comes from P4. The Ownership Map v1 Endpoints sheet has no contact-point endpoint at all, so the read and the maintenance write of the contact point have no contract in the target.
evidence: Source section 4 bullets; FSD P6 v3 A2.18 ('Contact values are read from v_ace_contact; consent, verification and failed count are held in recovery.contact_point_ext'); Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables (contact_point_ext to P1); TSD P6 v2 T5.2 ('P4 for access and reference data'); Ownership Map v1 sheet Endpoints (no contact-point row).
owner_role: Service owners of P6 rwb-comms and P1 rwb-source-data; product owner
proposed: Keep the contact point and its consent in P1 rwb_source_data.contact_point_ext as the owner of record, and have rwb-comms read and maintain it through a P1 contract that the P1 API specification publishes.

title: The sources name different sets of deviation codes that raise a contact stop
source: Recovery Workbench Notification and Correspondence Design v2.docx; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design v1
description: The source says a contact stop for a complaint, death or legal hold stops messages and letters except statutory notices where the law requires them. Rule R-LIT-05 says the contact stop is Y from X1 or X2 only. The Temporal and Drools design says the stop applies for X1 to X3, with X3 the deceased case. The design therefore does not know whether a death (X3) holds a notice.
evidence: Source section 4, second bullet; Routing Logic v4 row R-LIT-05 ('contact_stop = Y from X1 or X2'); Temporal and Drools Design v1 slide 8 notes ('Contact stop for X1 to X3').
owner_role: Service owners of P6 rwb-comms and S8 rwb-deviation; business lead
proposed: Read the stop as X1 to X3, which is the wider and the safer reading, keep the hold reason on the notice, and ask the business lead to correct R-LIT-05.

title: The notice approval sits in P6, P7 and S4 at once
source: Recovery Workbench Notification and Correspondence Design v2.docx; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5; Microservice Ownership Map v1
section: 2 How a notice is produced and 2.1, step 5
description: The source says the litigation officer approves the notice where the template requires approval. Architecture v5 slide 17 puts 'Decision: child: approval' in the OUT list of rwb-comms and gives the ApprovalWorkflow to P7. The Ownership Map v1 Endpoints sheet gives POST /notices/{noticeId}/approve to S4 rwb-litigation, and the Architecture v5 event catalogue has rwb-decision consume EV-13 NoticeGenerated. No source says which service holds the approval, which record is authoritative, or what the notice does while the approval is open.
evidence: Source section 2, fourth bullet; Architecture v5 slide 17 (P6 OUT: 'Decision: child: approval') and slide 14 (P7 IN: ApprovalWorkflow); Ownership Map v1 sheet Endpoints (POST /notices/{noticeId}/approve to S4); Architecture v5 slide 42 (EV-13 consumer rwb-decision).
owner_role: Service owners of P6 rwb-comms, P7 rwb-decision and S4 rwb-litigation
proposed: Hold the approval in P7 ApprovalWorkflow as a child of NoticeDispatchWorkflow, with the notice as its source, and keep POST /notices/{noticeId}/approve of S4 as the litigation officer's decision point. The notice waits in Approved and is not written to the file.

title: The case-level list of notices is named by Architecture v5 but has no endpoint row
source: Recovery Workbench Notification and Correspondence Design v2.docx; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5; Microservice Ownership Map v1
description: Architecture v5 slide 17 gives rwb-comms the REST operations POST /notices (request) and GET /cases/{id}/notices. The Ownership Map v1 Endpoints sheet holds POST /cases/{caseId}/notices and GET /notices/{noticeId} for P6 and no case-level GET. The design needs the case-level read, because the case screen shows the notices of a case, and it cannot name a path that a contract does not hold.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 17 and its note ('GET /cases/{id}/notices'); Ownership Map v1 sheet Endpoints (P6 rows: POST /cases/{caseId}/notices, GET /notices/{noticeId}, admin and template rows).
owner_role: Service owner of P6 rwb-comms; API owner
proposed: Keep the case-level list as a P6 operation and settle its path in the P6 API specification; until then read the notices of a case through GET /notices/{noticeId} per notice.

title: The partner instruction and the internal alert are rows of the design but are not rwb-comms notices in the target
source: Recovery Workbench Notification and Correspondence Design v2.docx; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5
description: Section 1 names five kinds, and two of them have another owner in the target: the partner instruction is issued by rwb-partner (S9) through the partner portal with FAPI 2.0, and the internal alert is a task of rwb-case (P3) read on the case timeline. The source does not say whether rwb-comms keeps a record of either, and the OUT list of rwb-comms in Architecture v5 names no partner or internal channel.
evidence: Source section 1 table rows 'Partner instruction' and 'Internal alert'; Architecture v5 slide 17 (S9 IN: Staff GET/POST /partners, /instructions; Partner portal /partner/v1/*) and slide 41 (P3 owns tasks and the timeline); Architecture v5 slide 17 P6 OUT list (WIN file, document, approval, integration, SMS and LINE).
owner_role: Service owners of P6 rwb-comms, S9 rwb-partner and P3 rwb-case
proposed: Record the partner instruction as S9 InstructionWorkflow and the internal alert as a P3 task; rwb-comms keeps the template of the partner instruction only and no record of the internal alert.

title: No event, job or window tells rwb-comms that a proof of delivery has arrived
source: Recovery Workbench Notification and Correspondence Design v2.docx; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5; Recovery Workbench Interface Specifications v4
section: 2 How a notice is produced and 2.1, step 7
description: The source says WIN returns the barcode and then the proof of delivery in the weekly file, and that the delivery date starts the notice period. In the target the weekly proof is INT-15, ingested by ACE and read by rwb-source-data through v_ace_pod. The Architecture v5 event catalogue has no proof-of-delivery event and no consumer row for a proof arrival, the job map names no inbound proof job or window, and rwb-comms consumes only EV-05, EV-06, EV-07, EV-10 and EV-12. The design cannot say how the notice learns that its proof has arrived.
evidence: Source section 2, sixth and seventh bullets; Interface Specifications v4 row INT-15 (inbound, weekly, ACE ingestion, read through v_ace_pod, owner P1); Architecture v5 slide 42 event catalogue (no proof event); Architecture v5 slide 44 job map (no proof inbound job); Architecture v5 slide 17 (P6 IN event list).
owner_role: Service owners of P6 rwb-comms and P1 rwb-source-data; integration owner
proposed: Read the proof through the P1 contract on the business date of the ACE batch, match it to the notice by barcode, and publish EV-15 NoticeDelivered from rwb-comms. No new event and no new job is invented.

title: Reference data is read from P4 in TSD P6 and from P3 in the plan default ruling
source: Recovery Workbench Notification and Correspondence Design v2.docx; Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1
description: The source says contact times and frequency follow the Debt Collection Act and bank policy, held as reference data. TSD P6 T5.2 says the module calls P3 for the case, P7 for the decision log, P4 for access and reference data, P5 for documents and P6 for notices. The plan default ruling gives reference data and LOV to P3 rwb-case, and DP-07 adds C RWB-P3-E1043-CON. Two services are named for the same data.
evidence: Source section 4, third bullet; TSD P6 v2 T5.2 ('P4 for access and reference data'); Rules v1 R3 default rulings ('Reference data, LOV | rwb-case') and R5.5 DP-07 ('Reference-data contract of rwb-case').
owner_role: Service owners of P3 rwb-case and P4 rwb-access; business lead
proposed: Follow R3 and DP-07: contact times and frequency are reference data of P3 rwb-case, read through C RWB-P3-E1043-CON. Access data, roles and DoA stay with P4.

title: The Compliance approval of customer wording has no artefact in the target template
source: Recovery Workbench Notification and Correspondence Design v2.docx; Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2; Microservice Ownership Map v1
description: The source says Legal counsel approves each version and Compliance approves customer wording. The target template row carries approved_by_legal, approved_by and approved_at, and POST /admin/templates/{templateId}/approve records the Legal approval with its valid-from date. No source names a field, a record or an approval step for the Compliance approval, so the second approval has nowhere to be recorded.
evidence: Source section 3 row 'Approval | Legal counsel approves each version; Compliance approves customer wording'; TSD P6 T3.1 template fields DF-REF-051, DF-REF-063 and DF-REF-064; TSD P6 API-P6-006 POST /admin/templates/{templateId}/approve; Ownership Map v1 sheet Endpoints.
owner_role: Service owner of P6 rwb-comms; Compliance and Legal roles
proposed: Record the Compliance approval as a second approval of P7 with the template as its source, and keep approved_by_legal on the template row for the Legal approval that the endpoint records.
